document.title: The 2008 Annual Report of the Board of Trustees of the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance and Federal Disability Insurance Trust Funds

II.C1.footnote_1: Ultimate values are assumed to be reached within 25 years. See chapter V for details, including historical values and projected values prior to reaching the ultimate.
II.C1.title: Ultimate Values of Key Demographic and Economic Assumptions for the Long-Range (75-year) Projection Period

V.A1.asadr_definition: Age-sex-adjusted death rate per 100,000: the crude rate that would occur in the enumerated total population as of April 1, 2000, if that population were to experience the death rates by age and sex observed in, or assumed for, the selected year (footnote 2).
V.A1.title: Principal Demographic Assumptions, Calendar Years 1940-2085

V.A3.note: Historical rows (through 2007; 2005-2007 footnote 2 'Estimated') carry one series printed under the intermediate columns.
V.A3.title: Period Life Expectancy

V.A4.note: At birth: for those born on January 1 of the year. At 65: for those attaining age 65 on January 1 of the year.
V.A4.title: Cohort Life Expectancy

V.B1.cpi_concept: Annual-average CPI-W growth by calendar year. This is not the COLA, which V.C1 reports on the third-quarter-over-third-quarter statutory basis (e.g. 2008: V.B1 CPI 2.8, V.C1 COLA 2.7).
V.B1.footnote_3: Historical data are not available for the full year [2007]. Estimated values vary slightly by alternative and are shown for the intermediate alternative.
V.B1.title: Principal Economic Assumptions
V.B1.units: Annual percentage change from the prior year for single-year rows; compound average annual percentage change for ranges (footnote 1). Real-wage differential: unrounded covered-wage growth less unrounded CPI growth (footnote 2).

columns.cola_percent: OASDI benefit increase (percent); footnote 1: effective with benefits payable for June in each year 1975-82, and for December in each year after 1982
columns.contribution_benefit_base: OASDI contribution and benefit base, dollars
columns.ret_exempt_at_nra: Retirement earnings test exempt amount, year of NRA, dollars
columns.ret_exempt_under_nra: Retirement earnings test exempt amount, under NRA, dollars

footnote_markers.6: Originally determined as 2.4 percent, but pursuant to Public Law 106-554, is effectively 2.5 percent.
footnote_markers.7: Actual amount, as determined under automatic-adjustment provisions.

V.C5.title: DI Beneficiaries With Benefits in Current-Payment Status at the End of Calendar Years 1960-2085

text_values.meaning: Ultimate annual CPI increase (V.B.2).
text_values.quote: The ultimate annual increases in the CPI are assumed to be 1.8, 2.8, and 3.8 percent for the low cost, intermediate, and high cost assumptions

text_values.meaning: Intermediate CPI path stated in V.B.2 (annual-average basis).
text_values.quote: For the intermediate assumptions, the annual change in the CPI is assumed to decrease from 2.8 percent for 2007 to 2.5 percent for 2009, then rise gradu- ally to the assumed ultimate rate of 2.8 percent for 2010 and later

text_values.meaning: Ultimate average covered wage growth (V.B.3).
text_values.quote: the assumed ultimate annual growth rates in the average covered wage are 3.4, 3.9, and 4.4 percent for the low cost, intermediate, and high cost assumptions

text_values.meaning: Span of historical death rates underlying TR2008 (V.A.2).
text_values.quote: Historical death rates (for years 1900-2004) used in developing estimates for this report

text_values.meaning: Ultimate average annual decline in the total age-sex-adjusted death rate, 2032-2082 (V.A.2).
text_values.quote: projected to decline at ultimate average annual rates of about 0.32 percent, 0.73 percent, and 1.21 percent between 2032 and 2082 for alternatives I, II, and III, respectively

text_values.meaning: Ultimate average annual decline in the age-sex-adjusted death rate at 65+, 2032-2082 (V.A.2).
text_values.quote: age-sex-adjusted death rates for ages 65 and over are projected to decline at average annual rates of about 0.28 percent, 0.65 percent, and 1.13 percent between 2032 and 2082 for alternatives I, II, and III, respectively

text_values.meaning: How TR2008 moves from observed 1984-2004 reductions to the 2032+ ultimate reductions (V.A.2). The age-group/cause-specific reductions themselves are not published.
text_values.quote: After 2004, the reductions in central death rates for alternative II are assumed to change rapidly from the average annual reductions by age group, sex, and cause of death observed between 1984 and 2004, to the ultimate annual percentage reductions by age group, sex, and cause of death assumed for 2032 and later. The reductions in death rates under alternatives I and III are also assumed to change rapidly to their ultimate levels, but start from lev- 1 Calculated here as the crude rate that would occur in the enumerated total population, as of April 1, 2000, if that population were to experience the death rates by age and sex for the selected year. 2 Average rate of decline is calculated as the annual geometric rate of reduction between the first and last years of the period. 75 Assumptions & Methods els which are, respectively, 50 or 150 percent of the average annual reduc- tions observed between 1984 and 2004

text_values.meaning: Average annual geometric decline in the age-sex-adjusted death rate, 2007-2082 (VI.D2).
text_values.quote: The age-sex-adjusted death rates decline at average annual rates of 0.30 percent, 0.75 percent, and 1.26 percent for alternatives I, II, and III, respectively

text_values.meaning: Timing of DI incidence assumptions (V.C.6.a).
text_values.quote: For the first 10 years of the projection period (through 2017) incidence rates reflect several factors including: (1) aspects of program administration (pro- cessing of the special disability workload described in section IV.A.2, efforts to reduce the disability backlog, and recent changes to how claims are adju- dicated); (2) assumed future unemployment rates; and (3) underlying trends in incidence. After 2017, age-sex-specific incidence rates are assumed to trend toward the ultimate rates assumed for the long-range projections, reaching these ultimate rates in 2027

text_values.meaning: Ultimate DI incidence (V.C.6.a).
text_values.quote: For the intermediate alternative, the ultimate age-sex-adjusted incidence rate (adjusted to the disability exposed population for the year 2000) for ages through 64 is assumed to be 5.2 awards per thousand exposed population. 2 This level is about 1 percent higher than the average rate for the historical period 1970 through 2007. The ultimate age-sex-adjusted incidence rates for the low cost and high cost alternatives are assumed to be 4.2 and 6.2 awards per thousand exposed
text_values.unit: awards per 1,000 disability-exposed (age-sex-adjusted to 2000 exposed population, ages through 64)

text_values.meaning: Intermediate DI death-termination rate, short range (V.C.6.b).
text_values.quote: the age-sex-adjusted death rate (adjusted to the 2000 disabled-worker population) under the intermediate assumptions is projected to gradually decline from 27.9 deaths per thousand 120 Program Assumptions and Methods beneficiaries in 2007 to about 23.9 per thousand by 2017

text_values.meaning: Intermediate DI recovery rate, short range (V.C.6.b).
text_values.quote: The age-sex- adjusted recovery rate under the intermediate assumptions is assumed to rise from a relatively low level of 10 per thousand beneficiaries in 2007 (reflect- ing temporarily lower levels of continuing disability reviews) to 12 per thou- sand beneficiaries by 2017

text_values.meaning: Short-range low/high-cost DI termination relative to intermediate (V.C.6.b).
text_values.quote: Under low cost (high cost) assumptions, total age-sex-adjusted termination rates due to death and recovery are assumed to increase (decrease) to levels roughly 10-15 percent higher (lower) than those under the intermediate assumptions

text_values.meaning: Base period of the long-range DI termination rates (V.C.6.b; footnote cites Actuarial Study 118).
text_values.quote: For the long-range period (post-2017), death and recovery rates are projected relative to rates by age, sex, and duration of entitlement over the base period 1996-2000

text_values.meaning: Ultimate DI recovery rates (V.C.6.b).
text_values.quote: The ultimate age-sex-adjusted recovery rate for disabled work- ers is assumed to be about 10.8 per thousand beneficiaries. Ultimate age-sex- adjusted recovery rates for low cost and high cost alternatives are assumed to reach about 13.1 and 8.6 recoveries per thousand beneficiaries, respectively. For all three sets of assumptions, the ultimate recovery rates are reached in the twentieth year of the projection period (2027)

text_values.meaning: DI death-termination rates in 2085 (V.C.6.b); death rates change at the same rate as general-population death rates.
text_values.quote: From the age-sex- adjusted death rate of 27.9 per thousand beneficiaries in 2007, rates of 21.4, 12.2, and 7.7 per thousand disabled-worker beneficiaries are projected for 2085 under the low cost, intermediate, and high cost assumptions

text_values.meaning: DI worker counts (V.C.6.d).
text_values.quote: The number of disabled workers in current-payment status is projected to grow from 7.1 million at the end of 2007, to 12.2 million, 14.1 million, and 14.8 million at the end of 123 Assumptions & Methods 2085, under the low cost, intermediate, and high cost assumptions
text_values.unit: millions of disabled workers in current-payment status

text_values.meaning: DI prevalence (V.C.6.d).
text_values.quote: The age-sex-adjusted disabled-worker prevalence rate for ages through 64 is projected to grow from 40.0 per thousand disability insured at the end of 2007, to 47.4 per thousand at the end of 2085 under the intermediate assump- tions. As mentioned above, the growth in prevalence is expected to slow rel- ative to the historical period. Under the low cost and high cost assumptions, the age-sex-adjusted disabil- ity prevalence rate is projected to decrease to 35.6 per thousand and increase to 59.6 per thousand insured workers at the end of 2085
text_values.unit: per 1,000 disability insured (age-sex-adjusted to 2000 insured population)

text_values.meaning: VI.D7 statement of ultimate DI incidence.
text_values.quote: In comparison to the his- torical period 1970 through 2007, the ultimate age-sex-adjusted incidence rate is 1 percent higher for alternative II, 19 percent lower for alternative I, and 20 percent higher for alternative III

text_values.meaning: VI.D8 statement of DI termination assumptions (age adjusted to disabled workers in current-payment status in 2000).
text_values.quote: For alternative II, the age-sex-adjusted 1 death rate is assumed to decline to a level at the end of the 75-year period that is about 56 percent lower than the level in 2007. For alternative I, the age-sex-adjusted death rate is assumed to decline to a level in 2085 that is about 23 percent lower than the level in 2007. For alternative III, the age-sex-adjusted death rate is assumed to decline to a level at the end of the 75-year period that is about 72 percent lower than the level in 2007. For all three alternatives, ultimate recovery-termination rates by age, sex, and duration are assumed to be attained in the twentieth year of the projec- tion period. For alternative II, the age-sex-adjusted1 recovery rate in 2027 is about 11 recoveries per thousand disabled-worker beneficiaries. For alternative I, the age-sex-adjusted recovery rate in 2027 is about 13 recover- ies per thousand disabled-worker beneficiaries. For alternative III, the age- sex-adjusted recovery rate in 2027 is about 9 recoveries per thousand dis- abled-worker beneficiaries

text_values.meaning: COLA effective-month convention and AWI continuation pointer (V.C1 footnotes 1-2).
text_values.quote: 1 Effective with benefits payable for June in each year 1975-82, and for December in each year after 1982. 2 See table VI.F6 for projected dollar amounts of the AWI beyond 2017.

text_values.meaning: Adjusted CPI index base (VI.F6 footnote 1).
